checks.requirement: Stay responsive and visible through representative motion and terrain
checks.evidence: Recorded planter failure repaired. Stationary baseline stayed supported; bounded visual-only target probe recovers, with 2 of 1468 updates withheld. This probe does not move the actual player. Three further probes captured one deadline refusal; subsequent three 20-second windows published all 2978 updates. A later passive 74-second diagnostic interval published/submitted all 3161 updates; sampled recording frames show stationary character and visible rug. Actual walking remains unverified.

checks.requirement: Bound hot-path work and avoid recurring faults or allocation-driven stalls
checks.evidence: 20-second timing/counter snapshots: initial window peak update/build 67.16/20.65 ms, subsequent 60 seconds peak 5.65/3.75 ms with 2978/2978 publications. One observed center-floor query deferral after a 6.36 ms one-ray update. Existing 2 ms query deadline and 100-ray cap retained; no new native query or geometry traversal in rejection diagnostics. Candidate .9 reuses private solver buffers/remap: warmed 361-vertex moving-grid solver allocations 12984 to 8784 bytes/frame, 21000 bytes saved per shift; mesh outputs remain independently owned. Two added regression tests preserve reference physics and bounded warm allocation. A 6.40 ms refusal still occurred; stage timings added to narrow future failures. Final candidate timing reproduction: player stage 0.024 ms, maintenance 6.309 ms, center 0.003 ms. Maintenance is isolated, but computation/JIT/GC/scheduling cause remains unproven.
